office_does: A State Senator writes and votes on Washington state law and the operating, capital and transportation budgets for a four-year term.
race_blurb: Two Republicans meet in the general for an open seat: Sen. Nikki Torres, who moved into the 8th after court-ordered redistricting, and Kennewick School Board President Gabe Galbraith. Their stated positions on taxes and public safety are close; the contrast is a Senate record and caucus leadership versus a local-roots challenger who centers parental rights.

candidates.summary: Four-year 15th District state senator and Republican Deputy Floor Leader, a former Pasco council member and credit-union business lender, running in the 8th after redistricting.
highlights: Voted against ESSB 6346, the 2026 tax on income over $1 million, and against the 2025 B&O, capital gains and services tax bills [S3][S4][S5][S6]
Voted for Initiative 2081 (2024) and against ESHB 1296 (2025), which amended the parents' bill of rights [S8][S9]
Prime sponsor of the 2025 school emergency-response law and the 2026 crash-prevention-zone law [S11][S12]
Pledges full police funding and changes to the 2021 police reform laws, including vehicle pursuits [S14]
Placed first in the primary with about 52% [S19]

taxes.basis: Voted no on ESSB 6346 and on the 2025 B&O (ESHB 2081), capital gains/estate (ESSB 5813) and services excise (ESSB 5814) tax bills; pledges to oppose 'unfair taxes'.

spending.basis: Voted against the 2025-27 operating budget and pledges conservative, responsible budgets and opposition to wasteful spending, while touting $500 million in regional capital funding.

safety.basis: Law-enforcement support is her lead accomplishment; pledges full police funding and rolling back 2021 police reform limits on pursuits; sponsored the school emergency-response law.

climate.basis: Opposes the fuel-price effect of the state carbon program and defends the Snake River dams, while saying dams and salmon recovery can coexist.

housing.basis: Voted against EHB 1217 rent-increase limits; proposes working with home builders on costs.

experience.basis: Four-year senator in caucus leadership and former city council member, facing a first-time legislative candidate.

parental-rights.basis: Voted for Initiative 2081 (unanimous in the Senate) and against ESHB 1296; no stated position on I-1.

candidates.summary: Kennewick School Board president, Marine veteran and Hanford security specialist making his first run for the Legislature on local roots and parental rights.
highlights: Says he was lead plaintiff in a lawsuit challenging HB 1296, the 2025 amendments to the parents' bill of rights [S4]
Opposes higher taxes and fees and pledges oversight of state spending [S1][S3]
Backed a sex-based girls'-sports position as school board president [S4]
Supports legislative hearings for citizen initiatives and opposes shifting power from elected sheriffs [S3]
Endorsed by the Benton County Republican Party [S1]

taxes.basis: Opposes higher taxes on working families and pledges to reduce taxes, fees and regulations; cites a school levy-rate cut.

spending.basis: Calls for smarter spending, real oversight and responsible budgets; cites the school district's financial rating.

safety.basis: Pledges full law-enforcement funding and enforcement on homelessness, paired with root-causes and treatment language.

climate.basis: All-of-the-above energy with nuclear, opposes dam breaching, and wants environmental policy that does not raise costs.

housing.basis: Wants more housing built faster and cheaper by cutting red tape.

experience.basis: First legislative run, framed against a 'political opportunist' and Olympia's status quo, though he has five years of elected school-board service.

local-control.basis: Opposes moving authority from elected sheriffs to state appointees and pairs housing supply with local control.

reform.basis: Supports the initiative process and public hearings for citizen initiatives; opposes legislative delay of them.

social.basis: Backed a school-district position that girls' sports eligibility be based on biological sex, including a federal complaint (self-reported).

parental-rights.basis: Makes parental rights a central plank; says he was lead plaintiff against HB 1296 and introduced a resolution against a student COVID-19 vaccine mandate; Parents' Rights in Education listed as supporter.
